doc: The kernel serves `place`; the user renames the folder (Finder, `mv`, a sync tool). Then a line arrives. User-visible questions: does the turn run; where does the transcript go — into the renamed folder, or into a ghost `.arbos/` recreated at the old path; does the window (a fresh attach) see the same history; and does the kernel say anything? A ghost at the old path is the destructive outcome: the user's history splits in two.

breaks.detail: the line typed after the rename went nowhere; the kernel stopped itself (stderr only) and nothing a person could read says the folder moved or the line was dropped
breaks.where: arbos-kernel serve: on a lost store, a last notice into the moved folder's transcript, or the desktop's respawn telling the user

kernel_stderr_says: arbos-kernel stopping: the place's .arbos store is gone (/tmp/arbos-qa-af-01-folder-renamed-under-a-running-kernel-ivb52iv_/place/.arbos); its jobs end with this kernel
